card.name: Reassuring or limiting phrases in drug labels
card.fires_on: Small linking words (at, in, is, if, may, do) that come right after an animal study or after a note about harmless appearance such as particles or color changes. They sit just before a dose limit or a statement that something is acceptable.

modes.label: Animal study dose limits
modes.description: The word "at" or "doses" after the animals studied, just before "doses up to".
modes.example: No evidence of carcinogenicity was found in two 2-year bioassays in rats<< at>> doses up to 100 mg

modes.label: Harmless appearance notes
modes.description: Linking words in statements that particles or color variation are normal or acceptable.
modes.example: There may be small white particles of protein in the solution. This<< is>> not unusual for proteinaceous solutions.

card.writes: Mostly unclear. The promoted tokens are Chinese words for innovation and a few English verbs, which do not fit this pattern.
card.plain: It fires on small connecting words just before a label says a dose limit or that something odd-looking is normal.
